newsitem.title: ITALY: BNL, INA outline Banco di Napoli plans.
newsitem.headline: BNL, INA outline Banco di Napoli plans.

text.p: Italian insurer INA and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) said on Wednesday that they could inject 1.2-1.3 trillion lire into Banco di Napoli after winning a controlling 60 percent stake in the southern bank.
The two partners also said in a joint statement that a fusion of Banco di Napoli and BNL was among the options under consideration.
The Treasury announced at the weekend that it had sold a 60 percent stake in Banco di Napoli to INA and BNL for 61.6 billion lire.
The government has said it wants to sell its remaining 40 percent holding in the troubled bank, which has lost some six trillion lire over the past three years, as soon as possible.
"The draft programmes assume capital interventions in favour of Banco di Napoli in the order of 1.2/1.3 trillion lire, much higher than those foreseen under current rules," the joint statement said.
Italian media reported at the weekend that Banco di Napoli needed recapitalisation of 900 billion lire to comply with capital adequacy ratios.

The joint statement said the capital increase would be met by INA and BNL in line with their respective stakes in the partnership of 51 percent and 49 percent. It made clear, however, that BNL could eventually fuse with Banco di Napoli.

"It is also envisaged that the activities of Banco di Napoli will be integrated strongly and rapidly with those of Banca Nazionale del Lavoro. Among the options being studied is the fusion of the two credit institutions," the statement said.
